newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran quakes kill 58, level 14 villages.
newsitem.headline: Iran quakes kill 58, level 14 villages.

text.p: Two earthquakes killed 58 people and levelled at least 14 villages in northeastern Iran where rescue teams were still searching for people among the rubble, state media said on Wednesday.
The official news agency IRNA put the death toll at 58 and said 153 people were injured in Tuesday's two quakes.
Tehran Radio said rescue workers were still digging in the rubble for survivors.
A total of 14 villages had been levelled and 45 others badly damaged in the quakes, one of which registered 5.6 on the Richter scale and the other 6.1, IRNA said.

It quoted Hassan Movahedian, governor of the provincial city of Bojnurd about 580 km (360 miles) northeast of Tehran, as saying there was no news from several villages because had cut off connecting roads.
The quakes had their epicentre in Bojnurd area, near the border with Turkmenistan and Iran's Caspian coast, which has an estimated population of 14,000 people.
The head of the geophysics institute of Mashhad University said it registered more than 100 aftershocks in nine hours on Tuesday, IRNA reported.

The governor said 500 tents, 4,000 blankets, five tonnes of rice, two tonnes of sugar, tea and vegetable oil as well as considerable amounts of clothing and heaters were immediately sent to the stricken region.
Tehran radio said on Tuesday relief efforts were being hampered by snow which had cut rural roads and by nightfall.

Iran's oil output and export operations were unaffected by the quakes which hit an area well away from the main oil province of Khuzestan in southwest Iran, the world's third largest oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway, Iranian and oil industry sources said.
Tremors of force six can cause widespread damage and those of force five are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in a densely populated area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
